messages:
alex_choi: Heads-up — I'm putting up a small proposal for changing how we treat long-tail SIEM exports and analyst access during incident triage. Goal: allow a scoped, read-only role for forensics that can access masked logs for up to 7 days post-incident, plus a strict KMS-unwrap JIT flow for any plaintext pulls. Want quick opinions before I open an RFC PR.

priya.desai: Can you spell out the scope? which log types, retention, and where the whitelist lives?

alex_choi: Quick sketch:
- Scope: auth/login, api-errors, and kube-audit only. No PII-heavy app logs (those stay masked).
- Retention: platform retention stays 90d; forensics role gets timeboxed access to a 7d snapshot exported to a secured bucket/consumer stream.
- SIEM consumer whitelist: explicit consumer IDs in our exporter config; external partners must be added per request template.
- KMS unwrap: requires a Jira ticket with approval and an entry in the audit table that includes approver, TTL, and reason.

jordan_w: Sounds reasonable. Two asks: 1) how do we prevent accidental bulk exports by the role? 2) can the unwrap be gated by a step function so we can revoke mid-flow?

alex_choi: For (1) the role is read-only and our exporter service will reject export calls that don't include the "export_context" header with a valid ticket id. For (2) yes — unwrap is a short-lived key grant created by the KMS-proxy that can be revoked; we can put it behind a Step Function so ops can cancel before it completes. Example exporter check:

```
# exporter config enforcement (pseudo)
if not request.headers.get('x-export-ticket'):
  return 403, 'missing ticket'
if not ticket_service.validate(ticket_id):
  return 403, 'bad ticket'
if not is_whitelisted_consumer(request.consumer_id):
  return 403, 'consumer not allowed'
```

samira_k: A couple security comments: 1) Require DLP scan for any export that includes free-form message fields; 2) Bind the forensics role to a purpose tag and timebox at the IAM level (7 days max) so we don't rely solely on process. 3) Audit events must record the KMS wrap/unwrap key id and requester identity.

priya.desai: Agree with samira. Also: add a human review step for external SIEM consumers — ops can't auto-approve partner requests. We'll need a little form in the support portal with required justification fields and a checklist (data minimality, SLA, legal ok).

alex_choi: Noted. I'll add those checks. I'm thinking the workflow looks like: request -> security review -> add consumer to whitelist -> ticket -> oncall triggers KMS-proxy unwrap (single use key) -> consumer pulls masked snapshot -> key auto-revokes.

oncall-bot: Incident ticket INC-4321 created by alex_choi for "forensics access test" — status: open — link: https://redwoodjira.example/browse/INC-4321 :ticket:

jordan_w: One more nit: ensure logs delivered to consumer are pre-scrubbed for email addresses and SSNs server-side. We should document accepted scrubbing rules in the exporter schema.

samira_k: I'll draft the audit field list and the IAM snippet. Also add a requirement that any external export must be encrypted at-rest with customer-managed keys where applicable.

alex_choi: Thanks. I'll spin up an RFC PR this afternoon and tag @priya.desai and @samira_k to review. If nobody objects by EOD I'll open the PR and drop the preliminary exporter config in it. :thumbsup:

priya.desai: Sounds good. If you can include a short checklist for SRE runbook changes (playbook for revoke + what to monitor) that'd help go faster.

alex_choi: Will do — adding SRE checklist to RFC.
